passage: In the school design lab, Lavanya looked at the tasks on the board for the model bridge: paint, wire the lights, test, build the frame. Vijay was ready to paint. "Not yet," said Lavanya. "Paint needs a dry frame, and the test can't happen until the wiring is done. Those two start the chain." She drew arrows: frame, then dry, then paint; circuit, then test. "Frame glue first, today, because it needs a whole day to dry. Circuit tomorrow. Meanwhile, Vijay, you can do the signboard and the poster. Nothing waits on those." Vijay shrugged, then began cutting card, his tongue between his teeth. By Friday the frame was dry and painted, and the little lights blinked on the first try.

qa.q: Why could Vijay not start painting at once?
qa.a: Painting needs a dry frame, and the frame glue needed a whole day to dry.

qa.q: How does Vijay feel when told not to paint yet?
qa.a: Vijay is a little reluctant and shrugs, but settles into the signboard work with concentration.

qa.q: What could Lavanya do if the glue takes longer than a day to dry, and why?
qa.a: Lavanya could move other tasks such as the poster and the wiring ahead while waiting, because independent jobs can run in parallel.

qa.q: How might Lavanya see Vijay being ready to paint?
qa.a: Lavanya sees the painting as coming too early, since paint needs a dry frame, so she gives Vijay the signboard and poster, which nothing waits on.

grounding: The leader sees that painting cannot start until the frame dries and testing needs a working circuit, so she starts those tasks first and lets independent ones run in parallel.

passage:
Dear Dilnaz,

Our model of a village bridge is finally on track, and I think I cracked why the last one wasn't.

Last time we all started with the fun bits. Someone painted, someone wired the lights, and then we found the painted parts had to be sanded off to glue the frame. Wasted a week.

This time I sat down on Sunday and asked: what has to wait for what? The frame needs two days to dry. Painting can't start till then. The LED lights can't be tested till the circuit works. But the poster and the written report don't need anything.

So on Monday, the very first thing, Faisal and I glued the frame. Rhea started the circuit the same day. Meanwhile Om wrote the report. By Thursday the frame was dry and painting began.

Nothing is waiting anymore. It feels almost too easy.

Love,
Nikita

qa.q: How long does the frame need to dry?
qa.a: The frame needs two days to dry.

qa.q: How does Nikita feel about the project now?
qa.a: Nikita feels relieved and quietly proud, even a bit surprised that it feels almost too easy.

qa.q: What else could Nikita plan for, now that the order is clear?
qa.a: Nikita could add a spare day before the deadline in case the paint or glue takes longer, since the whole chain depends on drying.

qa.q: How might Om see the new plan?
qa.a: Om likely feels less stressed, because the report could start on Monday without waiting for anyone else.

grounding: A letter shows a leader spotting which tasks depend on others, starting those first and letting independent ones run in parallel.

passage:
People think I was just bossy, Vinita, but no, there was a reason. Let me tell it properly.

I'm Irawati. Our Class 10 group had to build a working model of a water pump for the district exhibition in three weeks. Everyone wanted to start with the painting, because that's the fun part.

I drew the steps on a paper plate in the canteen. The wooden base had to be glued and left to set before anything went on it. The pump couldn't be tested until the motor circuit worked. The chart and the explanation card didn't depend on anything.

So I said: base and circuit start today, first. Chart people, start whenever. Painting waits.

Two of the girls sulked. But on day nine, the base was solid, the circuit ran, and we tested water flow. The group that started with paint was still waiting for glue at the exhibition.

qa.q: What did Irawati draw the steps on?
qa.a: Irawati drew the steps on a paper plate in the canteen.

qa.q: How did two of the girls feel when painting had to wait?
qa.a: They felt annoyed and sulky, because painting was the fun part and they had to hold off.

qa.q: What could Irawati say to make the order feel less bossy?
qa.a: Irawati could show the group the paper plate and explain the chain, so they see why painting waits instead of just being told.

qa.q: How might the girls who sulked see the plan by the exhibition?
qa.a: They would likely feel grateful and a bit sheepish, seeing their model tested while another group was still waiting for glue.

grounding: A spoken account of a leader starting tasks that others depend on first and letting independent tasks run alongside.
